title: Moscone 2007: Three Into One
description: Three products on one slide, a locked badge-door floor, and a gasp from the crowd—Go Deep into the morning a pocket ate three gadgets.
imageHint: A keynote stage, a black slab, and a crowd that forgot to breathe

questions.question: At Macworld on Jan. 9, 2007, which Apple CEO teased "an iPod, a phone, and an internet communicator"—then said they were one device?
questions.explanation: He repeated the trio three times, then: "Are you getting it? These are not three separate devices. This is one device." The room lost its mind.

questions.question: Jobs collapsed those three gadgets into what product name?
questions.explanation: He demoed music, mail, and a call from the stage. Prototypes had been so secret that teams worked behind locked badge doors.

questions.question: During that iPhone demo, Jobs placed an on-stage call to which Apple design chief sitting in the audience?
questions.explanation: Ive had steered the hardware toward a single slab of glass and aluminum. Hearing his phone ring in the house sealed the trick: it was real.

questions.question: Before that call to Jony Ive, Apple's secret phone effort ran under what color-coded project name?
questions.explanation: It began life closer to a tablet. Touch screens got good enough that the team flipped the idea into a phone—then spent years hiding it from the rest of the company.

questions.question: Project Purple launched with an exclusive U.S. carrier deal Jobs announced that morning. Which carrier?
questions.explanation: Still branded Cingular in some materials that week. Five years of exclusivity, a $499 price for the 4 GB model, and a line around the block.

deeperMode.title: Go Deeper: After the Gasp
deeperMode.description: The box, the fortune, and the OS that came home

questions.question: Jobs reportedly made the team redesign the first iPhone's packaging how many times?
questions.hint: He wanted the unboxing to feel like a ceremony

questions.question: Years earlier he had bought which animation studio from George Lucas—later his largest source of personal wealth?
questions.hint: Disney bought it in 2006 for stock

easterEgg.title: The first web server
easterEgg.text: Tim Berners-Lee built the Web's first server and browser on a NeXT cube. When Apple bought NeXT, that OS lineage became the heart of macOS—and of the iPhone Jobs unveiled at Moscone.
